rules.title: Seattle ban on algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services in connection with multifamily rental housing in Seattle. Violations carry penalties of up to $7,500 per violation.

coverage.summary: Applies to the use of specified 'coordinating services' in connection with Seattle multifamily properties. The source states no building-size, age or other coverage limits.
coverage.other_conditions: The ordinance's definition of 'coordinating service' and any exclusions are not captured in the documents provided.

rules.effective_date_note: The only source, a secondary law-firm alert, gives 'effective July 2025' (month only). The exact effective date is not in the documents. The law is in force as of the query date either way.
rules.quoted_span: Seattle’s ordinance expressly prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services and provides penalties of up to $7,500 per violation.
rules.review_note: Supported only by a secondary source (Morgan Lewis alert, Aug. 21, 2026). The official ordinance text, its exact effective date, definitions, exemptions and enforcement mechanism should be verified against the Seattle Municipal Code. The ordinance is at issue in Nicolas v. Essex Management Corp. and Romano v. UDR Inc. (W.D. Wash.). The alert also notes local algorithmic ordinances may face challenges to municipal authority.
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. It cites ch. 7.34.040 for both the prohibition and the penalties.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Prohibits specified coordinating services; penalties may reach $7,500 per violation
